keywords.def: The theory that the lithosphere is broken into plates that move over the asthenosphere.

en.text: The continents were once one Pangaea that broke apart and drifted. Plate tectonics explains how: lithospheric plates move on the asthenosphere, driven by convection, and meet at convergent, divergent and transform boundaries. Internal forces — folding, faulting, earthquakes and volcanism — build relief, and external forces — weathering, erosion, deposition and mass wasting — wear it down.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Pangaea → Laurasia + Gondwanaland → today's continents (continental drift, Wegener 1912).
Plate tectonics: plates on the asthenosphere; convection currents; convergent, divergent and transform boundaries.
Internal forces: folding, faulting, earthquakes, volcanism.
External forces: weathering, erosion, deposition, mass wasting.
Plate tectonics also shapes the oceans, atmosphere and long-term climate.

notes.text: Review Q3: the ocean around Pangaea was Panthalassa; Tethys lay between Laurasia and Gondwanaland, and the unit never mentions either. The item is reworded to ask about the sea between Laurasia and Gondwanaland.
